title: Μύρμηξ
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 240. Text as printed. Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Μύρμηξ ὁ νῦν τὸ πάλαι ἄνθρωπος ἦν· καὶ τῇ γεωργίᾳ προσέχων τοῖς ἰδίοις πόνοις οὐκ ἠρκεῖτο, ἀλλὰ καὶ τοῖς ἀλλοτρίοις ἐποφθαλμιῶν διετέλει τοὺς τῶν γειτόνων καρποὺς ὑφαιρούμενος.
sentences.tr: Myrmēx ho nyn to palai anthrōpos ēn· kai tēi geōrgiāi prosechōn tois idiois ponois ouk ērkeito, alla kai tois allotriois epophthalmiōn dietelei tous tōn geitonōn karpous hyphairoumenos.
sentences.l: The ant, the one of today, was in time long past a man; and applying himself to farming he was not content with his own labours, but casting his eye also upon what was other men's he went on stealing away the crops of his neighbours.
sentences.i: The ant we know now was once a man; he set himself to farming, was not content with what his own labour brought in, and kept an eye on what belonged to others, forever pilfering his neighbours' crops.
sentences.n: ὁ νῦν, 'the one now', with the article turning the adverb into a description — the ant as he is at present, against τὸ πάλαι, the matching adverbial accusative for the far past. ἀρκέομαι, 'be content', takes the dative of what contents one. διατελέω with a supplementary participle (ὑφαιρούμενος) means 'go on doing': the participle carries the action and the verb says only that it never stopped. ἐποφθαλμιάω, 'to set one's eye upon', takes the dative, as at fable 146, where greed likewise supplies the motive.

sentences.t: Ζεὺς δὲ ἀγανακτήσας κατὰ τῆς πλεονεξίας αὐτοῦ μετεμόρφωσεν αὐτὸν εἰς τοῦτο τὸ ζῷον ὃς μύρμηξ καλεῖται.
sentences.tr: Zeus de aganaktēsas kata tēs pleonexias autou metemorphōsen auton eis touto to zōion hos myrmēx kaleitai.
sentences.l: But Zeus, having grown indignant at his greed, transformed him into this animal which is called an ant.
sentences.n: ἀγανακτέω κατά with the genitive, 'to be angry against', as at fable 76 and fable 146 — the standing idiom when a god's patience runs out. The relative ὅς is masculine although its antecedent τὸ ζῷον is neuter: it has been drawn into the gender of μύρμηξ, the word that follows it. Chambry prints it so and it is left as printed.

sentences.t: Ὁ δὲ καὶ τὴν μορφὴν ἀλλάξας τὴν διάθεσιν οὐ μετεβάλετο· μέχρι γὰρ νῦν κατὰ τὰς ἀρούρας περιιὼν τοὺς ἄλλων πυροὺς καὶ κριθὰς συλλέγει καὶ ἑαυτῷ ἀποθησαυρίζει.
sentences.tr: Ho de kai tēn morphēn allaxas tēn diathesin ou metebaleto· mechri gar nyn kata tas arouras periiōn tous allōn pyrous kai krithas syllegei kai heautōi apothēsaurizei.
sentences.l: But he, having changed even his shape, did not alter his disposition; for down to now, going about over the ploughlands, he gathers up other people's wheat and barley and lays it up in store for himself.
sentences.i: But though his shape was changed, his disposition was not; for to this day he goes about the ploughland gathering up other men's wheat and barley and storing it up for himself.
sentences.n: τὴν μορφήν and τὴν διάθεσιν are the objects of the two verbs, set against each other: he changed the one, he did not change the other. μετεβάλετο is middle — the change would have had to be his own. περιιών is the participle of περίειμι, 'go about', from εἶμι 'go'. μέχρι νῦν pulls the story into the reader's own day — the fable's explanation is meant to be checked against the ants in the field.

sentences.t: Ὁ λόγος δηλοῖ ὅτι οἱ φύσει πονηροί, κἂν τὰ μάλιστα κολάζωνται, τὸν τρόπον οὐ μετατίθενται.
sentences.tr: Ho logos dēloi hoti hoi physei ponēroi, kan ta malista kolazōntai, ton tropon ou metatithentai.
sentences.l: The story shows that those who are wicked by nature, even if they are punished to the utmost, do not change their character.
sentences.n: φύσει is a dative of respect, 'in nature'; τὰ μάλιστα an adverbial accusative, 'to the utmost'. The whole moral is a near-twin of the one that closes the weasel's fable at 76, οἱ φύσει πονηροί … τὸν τρόπον οὐ μεταβάλλονται, with the concessive κἂν τὰ μάλιστα of the cat's fable at 14 standing in the middle of it. μετατίθεμαι in the middle is to shift one's own position, and so to change one's mind or one's ways.
